issues.legal_issue: The court-complaint requirement for forgery applies only when the offence is committed by a person in the capacity of a party to the proceeding, not when the forgery predates that person becoming a party.
material_facts: A sale deed was forged through the use of an impersonator before the revenue proceeding began.
The accused later relied on the deed in seeking a change to revenue entries.
The complainant initiated the criminal prosecution.
issues.conclusion: The prosecution for forgery was not barred for want of a complaint by the court in which the deed was later used; the time between the forgery and the deed’s later use was not controlling.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, read with Sections 190, 476, 476A and 476B, the restriction applies to specified offences committed by a party in that capacity. The court applied Patel Laljibhai Somabhai v. State of Gujarat, which approved the approach in Emperor v. Kushal Pal Singh: a forgery committed before the offender became a party is not brought within the restriction merely because the document is later used in a proceeding.

rule.if: prosecution_for_forgery and document_forged_before_proceeding and accused_not_yet_party_when_forgery_occurred and document_later_used_in_proceeding

predicates.prosecution_for_forgery: A criminal prosecution is brought for forgery.
predicates.document_forged_before_proceeding: The document was forged before the proceeding in which it was later used began.
predicates.accused_not_yet_party_when_forgery_occur: The accused had not yet become a party to the proceeding when the forgery occurred.
predicates.document_later_used_in_proceeding: The accused later used or produced the forged document in the proceeding.

issues.definition: When a forgery prosecution concerns a document forged before the accused became a party and later used in a proceeding, a private prosecution is not barred merely because the document was used there.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for abetting forgery may be sustained when the evidence establishes the accused’s assistance in procuring the forged document even though the person who physically forged it is not identified.
material_facts: The complainant denied executing the sale deed or appearing for its registration.
A fingerprint expert concluded that the thumb impression on the deed was not the complainant’s.
The accused maintained that the complainant had executed the deed, and two accused had identified the impersonator as the complainant.
One accused had obtained the deed and used it to seek a change to revenue entries.
The evidence did not identify who physically forged the deed.
issues.conclusion: The evidence supported the finding that all three accused abetted forgery, and the convictions under Sections 109 and 465 of the Penal Code were upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 109 and 465 of the Indian Penal Code apply where evidence establishes assistance or abetment in the commission of forgery. The person who physically made the forged document need not be identified for the accused’s abetment to be established. The court found the evidence, including the complainant’s denial, the fingerprint evidence, the false identification and the accused’s conduct concerning the deed, sufficient to leave no reasonable doubt.

rule.if: appeal_from_conviction_for_abetting_forgery and forged_document_used_to_claim_property and complainant_denied_executing_document and expert_excluded_complainant_fingerprint and accused_assisted_procurement_or_use

predicates.appeal_from_conviction_for_abetting_forg: The proceeding is an appeal from a conviction for abetting forgery.
predicates.forged_document_used_to_claim_property: A forged document was used to seek a claim or entry concerning property.
predicates.complainant_denied_executing_document: The person alleged to have executed the document denied executing it.
predicates.expert_excluded_complainant_fingerprint: An expert concluded that the fingerprint on the document was not that of the person alleged to have executed it.
predicates.accused_assisted_procurement_or_use: The accused assisted in procuring the document or knowingly used it to advance the property claim.

issues.definition: A conviction for abetting forgery may be sustained where an appeal concerns such a conviction and the evidence establishes that the accused assisted in procuring or using a forged property document despite the alleged executor’s denial and expert evidence excluding that person’s fingerprint.

issues.legal_issue: Sworn testimony by counsel about a fact connected with court proceedings may be relied on as evidence and is not excluded merely because an accused is not bound by counsel’s admissions.
material_facts: Counsel for the complainant testified that the complainant had affixed her specimen thumb impression to the relevant paper in his presence.
Counsel for the accused testified about his signature on that paper and the circumstances in which it was signed.
The trial court rejected reliance on counsel’s evidence in part on the ground that an accused is not bound by an admission made by counsel.
The High Court relied on the complainant’s testimony and the lawyers’ evidence in finding that the specimen impressions were hers.
issues.conclusion: The trial court was wrong to reject the lawyers’ sworn testimony on the ground that the accused were not bound by counsel’s admissions; the High Court was entitled to rely on testimony concerning what occurred in connection with the court proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: The rule that an accused is not bound by an admission made by counsel does not prevent the court from relying on counsel’s sworn testimony about a fact connected with proceedings in court. The court identified no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this evidentiary ruling.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is a criminal appeal from a conviction.
predicates.counsel_testified_under_oath_about_court: A lawyer gave sworn testimony about a fact connected with proceedings in court.
predicates.trial_court_rejected_testimony_as_nonbin: The trial court rejected the testimony on the ground that the accused was not bound by counsel’s admission.

issues.definition: When a lawyer gives sworn testimony about a fact connected with court proceedings, the testimony may be relied on even if the trial court rejected it as an admission that did not bind the accused.
